whyMetamorphic: I am interested in Metamorphic because the robotics role connects simulation, physical hardware, data collection, and applied ML research in one engineering loop. My graduate work has followed that same pattern across ROS/Gazebo motion planning, camera-LiDAR perception in CARLA, physical MiniDrone control, sensor fusion, logging, and repeatable validation. I would value the chance to build reliable simulation and hardware infrastructure that helps researchers move policies between experiments and real robots while preserving safety, calibration quality, and reproducibility.
exceptionalEffortAndPerseverance: During my Efficient TransFuser research project, mixed-precision training repeatedly failed because CenterNet focal loss became unstable under FP16. Rather than disabling the feature or treating it as random training noise, I isolated the failure by comparing task losses, precision modes, and intermediate values. I traced the issue to the numerical behavior of the focal-loss computation, tested the diagnosis, and implemented a stable correction while preserving the rest of the accelerated training pipeline. I documented the root cause and reran evaluations to confirm that the fix held across experiments. The experience reinforced a habit I bring to robotics work: reduce an ambiguous system failure into observable components, test one hypothesis at a time, and verify the repair at the system level.
